title: An open agentic AI co-scientist for clinical and biomedical discovery
zh_title: OpenScientist：开源智能体AI协科学家用于临床与生物医学发现
summary: 开源智能体AI协科学家OpenScientist可针对科学家提出的问题生成可验证、有数据支撑的分析，并在五个生物医学案例中由领域专家评估。
key_points: 开源智能体系统，输出可验证、数据可溯源的分析
五个生物医学案例由领域专家评估
数分钟完成原需数月人力的分析
含隐藏评估队列与外部队列验证的案例
reason: 开源智能体系统+领域专家多案例评估，含隐藏与外部队列，属重要档
abstract: Biomedical research is constrained by the time and domain expertise required to analyze increasingly large and complex datasets. Here we present OpenScientist, an open-source agentic AI co-scientist designed to address this gap by investigating scientist-defined queries and generating verifiable, data-grounded analyses. OpenScientist was evaluated by domain experts across five biomedical case studies, completing analyses in minutes that otherwise would take months of human time and expertise. It accurately quantified Alzheimer’s blood biomarker performance, generated a plasma proteomic survival model that predicted survival in a hidden-evaluation cohort, proposed a reproducible mechanism linking tau pathology to altered lysosomal acidification, generated multiple myeloma hypotheses validated in an external cohort with attenuated signal in randomized controls, and demonstrated concordance with an independent human analysis in a blinded, prespecified proteomic comparison. These results support the use of OpenScientist to assist biomedical data analysis in concert with human experts. To support research involving sensitive clinical datasets, OpenScientist can operate in a fully air-gapped environment using open-source models for inference. OpenScientist demonstrates that open, auditable, agentic AI can support real-world clinical research by researching the literature, generating hypotheses, executing analyses, and generating insights from complex datasets.
zh_abstract: 生物医学研究受到分析日益庞大和复杂数据集所需时间和领域专业知识的制约。在此，我们介绍 OpenScientist，一种开源智能体式 AI 协同科学家，旨在通过研究科学家定义的查询并生成可验证、以数据为基础的分析来弥合这一差距。OpenScientist 由领域专家在五项生物医学案例研究中进行了评估，可在数分钟内完成原本需要数月人工时间和专业知识才能完成的分析。它准确量化了阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer’s）血液生物标志物的性能，生成了一个血浆蛋白质组学生存模型，该模型在隐藏评估队列中预测了生存，提出了一个将 tau 病理与溶酶体酸化改变联系起来、可重复的机制，生成了多发性骨髓瘤假设并在外部队列中得到验证，且在随机对照中信号减弱，并在一项盲法、预先设定的蛋白质组学比较中显示出与独立人工分析的一致性。这些结果支持使用 OpenScientist 与人类专家协同辅助生物医学数据分析。为支持涉及敏感临床数据集的研究，OpenScientist 可在使用开源模型进行推理的完全气隙隔离环境中运行。OpenScientist 表明，开放、可审计的智能体式 AI 可以通过检索文献、生成假设、执行分析并从复杂数据集中生成洞见来支持真实世界临床研究。

title: Dual chain-of-thought AI‑PDCA framework for clinical history taking and documentation
zh_title: 双链式思维 AI-PDCA 框架用于临床问诊与病历书写
summary: npj Digital Medicine 同行评审研究：构建双链式思维大模型支持的 PDCA 教学框架，并比较 AI 评分与教师评分的可靠性。
key_points: 构建双 CoT 大模型驱动的 PDCA 问诊训练框架
对 135 名医学生教育数据做回顾性观察分析

reason: 同行评审、方法有新意，但单中心回顾性、样本 135、仅内部对照
abstract: Clinical history-taking and documentation are foundational competencies in undergraduate medical training, yet scalable and individualized training tools remain limited. Large language model (LLM)-based systems provide automated practice opportunities but often lack structured medical reasoning, closed-loop instructional design, and integration into formal curricula. As part of a curriculum reform initiative, we constructed a clinical case repository, developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-integrated faculty Plan–Do–Check–Act (PDCA) training framework supported by dual chain-of-thought (CoT)-driven LLMs, and evaluated the reliability of AI-based scoring against faculty assessment. We then conducted a retrospective observational analysis of routinely collected educational performance data from 135 undergraduate medical students enrolled in one of three existing instructional configurations: traditional instruction, AI-assisted training, or AI + PDCA training. Educational outcomes were assessed using standardized Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) assessments. The AI + PDCA configuration was associated with the highest OSCE performance in both history-taking and clinical documentation. Among the two AI-supported configurations, longitudinal mixed-effects modeling showed steeper learning trajectories in the AI + PDCA configuration than in the AI-assisted configuration. These findings suggest that integrating AI-derived learning analytics with faculty-guided instructional intervention may support a closed-loop educational model associated with favorable competency acquisition while maintaining human oversight. This framework offers a scalable approach for implementing trustworthy, competency-based AI-enhanced medical education in routine academic practice.
zh_abstract: 临床病史采集和病历记录是本科医学培训中的基础胜任力，但可扩展且个体化的培训工具仍然有限。基于大语言模型（LLM）的系统提供了自动化练习机会，但往往缺乏结构化的医学推理、闭环教学设计以及整合到正式课程中。作为课程改革举措的一部分，我们构建了一个临床病例库，开发了一个整合人工智能（AI）的教师 Plan–Do–Check–Act（PDCA）培训框架，并由双思维链（CoT）驱动的 LLM 支持，同时评估了 AI 评分相对于教师评估的可靠性。随后，我们对 135 名本科医学生常规收集的教育表现数据进行了回顾性观察性分析，这些学生分别接受三种现有教学配置之一：传统教学、AI 辅助培训或 AI + PDCA 培训。教育结局使用标准化客观结构化临床考试（OSCE）评估来评价。AI + PDCA 配置在病史采集和临床病历记录方面均与最高的 OSCE 表现相关。在两种 AI 支持的配置中，纵向混合效应模型显示，AI + PDCA 配置的学习轨迹比 AI 辅助配置更陡峭。这些发现表明，将 AI 衍生的学习分析与教师指导的教学干预相结合，可能支持一种与良好胜任力获得相关的闭环教育模式，同时保持人类监督。该框架为在日常学术实践中实施可信、基于胜任力的 AI 增强医学教育提供了一种可扩展的方法。

title: Evidence-Conditioned Completion and Synthesis of Electronic Health Records
zh_title: EHRDiB：以证据为条件的电子病历补全与合成
summary: 预印本提出统一病历补全与合成的扩散桥框架，在MIMIC-IV与Duke Health上对比11种方法并评估效用与泄露风险。
key_points: 统一访视补全与病历合成，区分原始缺失与人为隐藏
8项补全对比中7项与真实数据分类器差距最小
合成任务AUPRC差距缩小45.2%，并评估泄露风险
reason: 方法有新意且双数据源对比充分，但为预印本、无临床结局与代码说明，属值得一看档
abstract: Patient information can guide electronic health record (EHR) generation, but how its amount shapes predictive utility and disclosure risk remains poorly characterized. Here we present EHRDiB, which unifies visit completion and synthesis by distinguishing original missingness from withheld inputs and combining a shared multimodal representation with an evidence-conditioned latent diffusion bridge. We compared EHRDiB with three completion and eight synthesis methods on MIMIC-IV and numerical and discretized Duke Health representations. Evaluation covered downstream predictive utility, generative diversity, and distributional fidelity for both tasks, and disclosure risk for synthesis. EHRDiB achieved the smallest utility gaps from real-data-trained classifiers in seven of eight completion comparisons. In synthesis, AUPRC gaps were 45.2% smaller for ten MIMIC-IV principal-diagnosis targets and 53.3% smaller for numerical Duke Health data relative to the best comparator. Synthesis with calibrated thresholding yielded the lowest marginal distribution error across all three datasets, with Coverage above 0.95 for both output rules. Across twelve evidence-fraction intervals in MIMIC-IV synthesis, membership-inference AUROC increased from 0.516 to 0.598 as the mean target evidence fraction rose from 0.20 to 0.50; utility gaps narrowed relative to the lowest evidence configuration but did not decrease monotonically. Our study provides a unified framework and empirical foundation for EHR generation that considers both its utility for clinical analysis and its information disclosure risk.
zh_abstract: 患者信息可以指导电子健康记录（EHR）生成，但其数量如何塑造预测效用和披露风险仍鲜有刻画。在此，我们提出 EHRDiB，它通过区分原始缺失与保留不提供的输入，并将共享多模态表示与证据条件化的潜在扩散桥相结合，统一了就诊完成和合成。我们在 MIMIC-IV 以及数值型和离散化 Duke Health 表示上，将 EHRDiB 与三种补全方法和八种合成方法进行了比较。评估涵盖两项任务的下游预测效用、生成多样性和分布保真度，以及合成任务的披露风险。在八项补全比较中的七项中，EHRDiB 相对于真实数据训练的分类器取得了最小的效用差距。在合成中，相对于最佳比较方法，十个 MIMIC-IV 主要诊断目标的 AUPRC 差距缩小了 45.2%，数值型 Duke Health 数据的 AUPRC 差距缩小了 53.3%。采用校准阈值化的合成在全部三个数据集上产生了最低的边缘分布误差，两种输出规则的 Coverage 均高于 0.95。在 MIMIC-IV 合成的十二个证据比例区间中，随着平均目标证据比例从 0.20 升至 0.50，成员推断 AUROC 从 0.516 增至 0.598；相对于最低证据配置，效用差距缩小，但并未单调下降。我们的研究为 EHR 生成提供了一个统一框架和实证基础，同时考虑其对临床分析的效用及其信息披露风险。

title: BioLT: Streaming Biosignal Modeling
zh_title: BioLT：面向长程生理信号的流式建模框架
summary: 预印本提出流式解码器框架，把窗口级生理信号模型转为可处理数小时长程ECG、PPG、EEG的模型。
key_points: 将任意窗口级特征提取器或基础模型转为流式模型
显式编码窗间时间间隔以建模信号中断
固定大小压缩记忆库使训练与推理保持线性
reason: 方法具新意并针对真实长程信号短板，但为预印本、未见外部验证细节，属值得一看档
abstract: AO_SCPLOWBSTRACTC_SCPLOWClinical biosignals such as ECG, PPG, and EEG are increasingly acquired as hours-long streams from bedside monitors and wearables, yet existing analysis pipelines almost universally operate on isolated short windows of around 10 seconds and cannot process the long, irregular, frequently interrupted signals. We introduce BioLT, a streaming decoder-only framework for long-context biosignal modeling that turns any window-level feature extractor or pretrained biosignal foundation model into a streaming model. BioLT combines (i) a discontinuity-aware encoding that exposes the inter-window elapsed time as an explicit input channel, so that the decoder can learn to model these gaps as clinically meaningful information, and (ii) a fixed-size compressed memory bank supervised with cumulative summary statistics, which keeps both training and inference linear in the recording length while preserving long-range context. We evaluate on CPSC-2021, VitalDB, MC-MED, and CHB-MIT for arrhythmia, sepsis, and seizure detection and for forecasting up to 20 minutes ahead, using domain features and embeddings from six biosignal foundation models. Across 21 dataset-feature settings, BioLT achieves the highest detection AUROC in 15 and the highest 20-minute forecasting AUROC in 13 settings, and shows consistent performance gains over state-of-the-art snapshot foundation-model embeddings. These highlight the importance of modeling how streaming biosignal representations evolve over time, beyond improving window-level representations alone.
zh_abstract: 临床生物信号（如 ECG、PPG 和 EEG）越来越多地以长达数小时的流形式从床旁监护仪和可穿戴设备中采集，但现有分析流程几乎普遍只处理约 10 秒的孤立短窗口，无法处理长时、不规则且频繁中断的信号。我们提出 BioLT，一种用于长上下文生物信号建模的流式仅解码器框架，可将任意窗口级特征提取器或预训练生物信号基础模型转换为流式模型。BioLT 结合了：(i) 不连续性感知编码，将窗口间经过时间作为显式输入通道暴露出来，使解码器能够学习将这些间隔建模为具有临床意义的信息；(ii) 一个固定大小的压缩记忆库，由累积汇总统计量监督，使训练和推理在记录长度上保持线性，同时保留长程上下文。我们在 CPSC-2021、VitalDB、MC-MED 和 CHB-MIT 上评估心律失常、脓毒症和癫痫发作检测以及最长提前 20 分钟的预测，使用领域特征和来自六个生物信号基础模型的嵌入。在 21 个数据集-特征设置中，BioLT 在 15 个设置中取得最高检测 AUROC，在 13 个设置中取得最高 20 分钟预测 AUROC，并相较于最先进的快照基础模型嵌入表现出持续的性能提升。这些结果突显了建模流式生物信号表示如何随时间演变的重要性，而不仅仅是改进窗口级表示。

title: Artificial Intelligence in Coronary Artery Disease: From Detection to Precision Management.

abstract: [Methodist DeBakey cardiovascular journal] Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, yet the landscape is rapidly evolving as artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to its detection, diagnosis, and management. This review surveys the expanding role of AI across the full spectrum of CAD care. In screening, deep-learning electrocardiography and electronic health record-based digital markers enable earlier identification of clinically significant disease. In noninvasive imaging, AI-driven coronary computed tomography angiography automates calcium scoring, derives fractional flow reserve without invasive wires, and quantifies high-risk plaque features that predict incident adverse events. Within the cardiac catheterization laboratory, angiography-derived physiologic assessment and AI-guided intravascular imaging segmentation support real-time procedural decision-making. Beyond diagnosis, machine-learning models integrating multimodality imaging data improve risk stratification over conventional clinical scores, while pharmacogenomic algorithms and wearable-based digital rehabilitation platforms enable patient-centric secondary prevention. Despite this progress, significant challenges persist, including limited evidence from randomized trials, algorithmic bias in underrepresented populations, regulatory uncertainty surrounding software-as-a-medical-device frameworks, and the risk of clinician de-skilling. AI has the potential to act as a collaborative tool that augments-rather than replaces-physician judgment. Future directions include foundation models, multiomics integration, agentic AI workflows, and equity-centered deployment strategies to ensure that AI-driven advances benefit all individuals with CAD.
zh_abstract: [Methodist DeBakey 心血管杂志] 冠状动脉疾病（CAD）仍是全球首要死因，但随着人工智能（AI）越来越多地应用于其检测、诊断和管理，这一格局正在迅速演变。本综述概述了 AI 在 CAD 诊疗全谱系中日益扩大的作用。在筛查方面，深度学习心电图和基于电子健康记录的数字标志物能够更早识别具有临床意义的疾病。在无创影像方面，AI 驱动的冠状动脉计算机断层扫描血管造影可自动进行钙化评分、无需侵入性导丝即可推导血流储备分数，并量化可预测新发不良事件的高危斑块特征。在心导管实验室中，血管造影衍生的生理学评估和 AI 引导的血管内影像分割支持实时术中决策。除诊断外，整合多模态影像数据的机器学习模型较传统临床评分改善风险分层，而药物基因组学算法和基于可穿戴设备的数字康复平台使以患者为中心的二级预防成为可能。尽管取得这些进展，重大挑战仍然存在，包括随机试验证据有限、代表性不足人群中的算法偏倚、围绕软件即医疗器械框架的监管不确定性，以及临床医生技能退化的风险。AI 有潜力作为一种协作工具，增强而非取代医生的判断。未来方向包括基础模型、多组学整合、智能体式 AI 工作流以及以公平为中心的部署策略，以确保 AI 驱动的进展惠及所有 CAD 个体。

abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Korea University Anam Hospital; conditions: AF - Atrial Fibrillation; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 1006; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common type of irregular heartbeat in adults. People with AF may also have other heart problems, including reduced heart pumping function or diseases affecting the heart muscle or heart valves. Identifying these problems early is important because the condition of the heart can affect treatment decisions and long-term care. An ultrasound examination of the heart, called transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) or an echocardiogram, is commonly used to check how well the heart pumps blood and to look for structural problems, such as heart valve disease. However, an echocardiogram requires special equipment and trained healthcare professionals to perform and interpret the examination. Because of these requirements, it may not always be available when needed. This can be particularly challenging in situations where heart function needs to be evaluated quickly, such as when a patient with AF has a very fast heart rate. Delays may also occur in outpatient settings because of limited availability of echocardiography. Artificial intelligence (AI) technology may provide an additional way to identify patients who are more likely to have heart problems and who may benefit from further evaluation. A standard 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) is a simple and widely available test that records the electrical activity of the heart. AI-based computer programs can analyze information contained in an ECG that may not be easily recognized through routine interpretation. This study will use two AI-based ECG programs, called AiTiALVSD and AiTiALVDD. AiTiALVSD analyzes a standard 12-lead ECG to identify patients who may have reduced heart pumping function. Previous studies have evaluated this program in different clinical settings, including patients with AF and a fast heart rate. AiTiALVDD analyzes the ECG for signs that may be associated with difficulty in the heart relaxing and filling with blood. Problems with heart relaxation and filling may occur in several types of heart disease, including heart valve disease, abnormal thickening of the heart muscle, heart disease related to high blood pressure, diseases affecting the heart muscle, and coronary artery disease. Importantly, some patients may have these conditions even when the heart's overall pumping function is normal. Therefore, evaluating only pumping function may not identify all patients who have important underlying heart disease. By using AiTiALVSD and AiTiALVDD together, this study
